questions.stem: Which multiplication has the same answer as 3 + 3 + 3 + 3 + 3?
questions.stemText: Which multiplication has the same answer as 3 + 3 + 3 + 3 + 3 ?
questions.explain: Count the 3s: there are 5 of them, so this is 5 groups of 3, which is 5 × 3 = 15. Counting one group too many gives 6 × 3, which is 3 too much, and multiplying the wrong pair gives 3 × 3 or 6 × 5. Multiplication is a short way of writing the same number added over and over - that is the whole idea, and it is why the times tables are worth knowing by heart.

questions.stem: Xin Yi works out 4034 + 1708 in columns. One column makes 12, so she writes 2 in that column and a small 1 above the column on its left. How much is that small 1 worth?
questions.stemText: Xin Yi works out 4034 + 1708 in columns. One column makes 12, so she writes 2 in that column and a small 1 above the column on its left. How much is that small 1 worth?
questions.explain: The column that makes 12 is the ones column: 4 + 8 = 12, and no other column reaches ten. 12 ones is 1 ten and 2 ones, so the 2 stays in the ones column - worth 2 - and the small 1 goes above the tens column - worth 10. The small 1 is worth 10. A mark is worth the column it is written in, not the digit it looks like: that is what regrouping means, ten of something small becoming one of the next size up. Every wrong answer here is one of the two slips - the right digit read in the wrong column, or the wrong digit read in the right one.

questions.stemText: Kavitha works out 82 + 84 in her head. She makes 90 first. 82 + 84 = 90 + ?
questions.explain: To get from 82 up to 90 you need 8, so 8 is moved across from the 84. That leaves 84 − 8 = 76, and 90 + 76 = 166. Whatever you give to one number you must take off the other, or the total changes. You could have rounded the 84 up to 90 instead and taken that amount off the 82: it is the same total either way, so it lands on the same answer.

questions.stemText: Which of these fractions is between 2/6 and 7/12?
questions.explain: Step 1: the two ends are not written in the same size of piece, so cut 26 into 12ths first: 2 × 2 = 4 and 6 × 2 = 12, so 26 is the same amount as 412. Step 2: now every fraction is in 12ths, so just count the tops - the answer has to be more than 4 of them and fewer than 7. questions.explain: Buying 5 tubs of cookies one by one costs 5 × $3 = $15, but 5 for $13 is cheaper, so buy as many bundles as you can. 13 ÷ 5 = 2 remainder 3, so 2 bundles cost 2 × $13 = $26. questions.stemText: A bag of rice is 5 times as heavy as a bag of sugar. Together they weigh 2 kg 400 g. How much heavier is the bag of rice than the bag of sugar, in g?
questions.explain: Draw a model. The bag of sugar is 1 unit and the bag of rice is 5 units, so together they are 6 units. Change to g: 2 kg 400 g = 2400 g. 1 unit = 2400 ÷ 6 = 400 g. The bag of rice has 5 - 1 = 4 more units than the bag of sugar: 4 × 400 = 1600 g.
